source.title: Double descent without digital computation.
source.authors: Sam Dillavou; Jason W. Rocks; Jacob F. Wycoff; Andrea J. Liu; D. Durian

record.file_problem: Full paper is present. There are minor PDF-extraction artifacts in equations, figure text, and page breaks, but they do not prevent reading the study.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests double descent by varying training-set size and measuring test loss, using an analog physical network and small digital networks rather than the original deep-network model-size sweep.
record.gate_note: The study varies training-set size, measures test classification error and hinge loss, and reports test-output variation. Training-loss curves are not included as separate rows because they do not measure the test-error outcomes named in the versions. Comparisons cited from other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study varies training-set size in a new setting, a self-training analog resistive network plus small digital networks. It reports test hinge loss rising and then falling around the point where training error vanishes, which bears directly on V3 (more data can hurt). It also reports output variation peaking at that transition (part of V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that an analog self-learning resistive network shows double descent in test hinge loss versus training-set size, but only with overclamping. They tie the peak to a spike in output variation at the transition where training error vanishes. They explain the unexpected peak location (γ≈6.4) by low input dimension and bounded, positive-only parameters, and propose the transition as a hardware benchmark of effective parameters.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a physical, decentralized resistive network with contrastive local learning and overclamping, and varies training-set size rather than deep-network model size. Digital comparisons use small two-layer classifiers and a shifted hinge loss.
record.method_sensitivity: The double-descent signal depends on using overclamping: the reported result is absent without it. The outcome also depends on the metric: test hinge loss is non-monotonic, whereas test classification error is monotonic. Peak location differs between the 2-feature setting and the reported 16-feature setting.

fits_no_version.finding: In the physical network and in 2-feature digital nets, the peak occurs far from the interpolation prediction, at γ≈6.4 and γ≈2 rather than γ=1/2. The authors attribute this to low feature dimension (finite-size effects) and to bounded, positive-only parameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The location of the sample-wise double-descent peak shifts from the parameter-count prediction in low-dimensional or parameter-constrained systems.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
record.problems: The physical experiment uses a single fixed network size and a single task, varies sample size, and uses a fixed 7% label-flip rate. The classification-error metric does not show double descent. The without-overclamping comparison has much higher training error. Digital-curve values are largely figure-only, and uncertainty is not stated for the digital simulations.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying test-error rows were left out. Training-error curves and cited results from other studies were excluded because they do not measure the test-error outcomes as separate results of this claim.

untested.parts: All of it. The physical network has a fixed size. The digital comparisons vary P only to locate the sample-wise peak; they do not report test error versus model size at fixed data.
All of it. No test error over epochs is reported.
All of it. There is no capacity sweep past interpolation across model classes.
All of it. Effective parameters are discussed as a hypothesis, but no single complexity measure is tested across axes.
Three parts: dependence on label-noise level (fixed at 7%), multiple or split peaks, and disappearance under optimally tuned regularization. Ridge was set to match peak height, not optimized.
All of it. Effective parameter count is invoked only to explain the peak location, not to recast the curve as a U-shape.

missing.locator: Digital Comparison; Fig. 4B inset; Appendix D Fig. 7B inset

missing.what: CLLN training hinge loss drops to zero at small M, around the test-loss peak, which marks the interpolation threshold.

record.verdict_notes: The study varies sample size, not model size. Its V3 evidence is the rise in test loss from M≈2 to M=5 before the drop. Tranche is set to T3 (new setting: physical analog hardware) rather than the record's T2. The no-overclamping result is labelled limits_scope, not challenges: the system there fails to reach low training error, so it is not tested at the interpolation threshold. Regularization in the digital nets was tuned to match peak height, not optimized, so it does not bear on V6's regularization claim.

versions.untested_parts: The physical network is fixed in size; the study does not sweep deep-network model size.
The study does not report test error over training epochs.
The study varies sample size in one binary classification task, with a fixed 7% training-label-flip rate; it does not test other noise levels or datasets.
The study does not sweep model capacity across model classes past an interpolation point. Its digital comparisons vary sample size, not capacity.
The study discusses effective parameters and compares peak locations, but does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample axes.
The study reports an output-variation spike around the test-loss peak, but does not vary label noise, test for multiple or split peaks, or test disappearance under optimally tuned regularization.

The study discusses effective parameter counts and hardware parameter restrictions, but does not show that measuring against an appropriate effective parameter count turns the second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.stage_stated: trained until gate voltages reach a steady value or training error drops to zero
rows.operation_detail: Varied training-set size M from 1 to 64 and measured test hinge loss after training.
rows.value: Strongly non-monotonic in γ=P/M, with a peak at γ=32/5; it drops sharply when parameters greatly exceed training points.
rows.uncertainty: Standard error; all error bars are smaller than the markers.
rows.note: The authors identify the test hinge-loss peak as double descent. γ=32/5 is stated as the peak location.
rows.check: Link and state are correct. Test hinge loss peaks at M=5 (γ=32/5), so adding samples from M≈2 up to 5 raises test loss. The authors place the peak at the transition where training error vanishes.
